[2026-08-27T02:07:48.183Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7722b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":67980,\"title\":\"Blazor Web: exception during WASM root component activation is silently discarded — InteractiveAuto page stays a dead prerender with no error and no Server fallback\",\"body\":\"### Is there an existing issue for this?\\n\\n- [x] I have searched the existing issues\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\n`WebAssemblyRenderer.OnUpdateRootComponents` fire-and-forgets the root component activation tasks:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/release/10.0/src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly/src/Rendering/WebAssemblyRenderer.cs#L72-L84\\n\\n```csharp\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Add:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.AddRootComponentAsync(...);\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Update:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.UpdateRootComponentAsync(...);\\n```\\n\\nIf activation throws (component constructor, DI resolution, a type-initializer failure in a dependency that only fails under Mono WASM, …), the fault is completely swallowed:\\n\\n- nothing in the browser console (no unhandled rejection, no `Blazor` error),\\n- no `blazor-error-ui`,\\n- no `ILogger` output,\\n- and for `InteractiveAuto`, **no fallback to Server**, even though the Server registration of the same page works (prerendering proves it).\\n\\nThe user is left on a permanently dead prerender. Worse: once Auto has committed to WebAssembly (runtime cached), even a **full page reload** of the affected page re-attempts WASM activation and dies the same way — there is no user-side recovery short of clearing the cache.\\n\\n**Real-world impact:** we hit this in production when a `TypeInitializationException` was thrown while constructing a ctor-injected DI service during activation of an `InteractiveAuto` page — but any exception thrown during activation triggers it; the specific trigger is irrelevant. Because the fault is discarded, diagnosing the underlying application-side bug took a multi-day investigation across CI bisects and Playwright traces, and ultimately required attaching an `AppDomain.FirstChanceException` handler in the WASM client — that handler is the only place the exception is observable. With ordinary error surfacing, the root cause would have been visible in the first failing run\\u0026#39;s browser console.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nSome combination of:\\n\\n1. The activation fault is logged (console + `ILogger`) and surfaces `blazor-error-ui`, like unhandled exceptions elsewhere in Blazor.\\n2. For `InteractiveAuto`, a failed WebAssembly activation falls back to the Server render mode instead of leaving a dead prerender (the server was able to render the page seconds earlier).\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nMinimal repro (unmodified `dotnet new blazor -int Auto` template plus only the changes listed in its README): https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-dotnet--aspnetcore-wasm-silent-activation\\n\\nA service is registered working on the server and with a throwing factory in the WASM client:\\n\\n```csharp\\n// Client Program.cs — simulates a dependency that only fails on the WASM runtime\\nbuilder.Services.AddSingleton(_ =\\u0026gt;\\n    throw new InvalidOperationException(\\u0026#34;Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.\\u0026#34;));\\n```\\n\\n1. `dotnet run`, open `/counter` — first interactive visit renders Interactive **Server**.\\n2. Navigate Home ↔ Counter until Counter reports **WebAssembly** (Auto committed to WASM).\\n3. Click the nav link to `/crash` (enhanced navigation), a page that injects the service.\\n4. Observe: page reports `RendererInfo: Static, IsInteractive: false` forever; button does nothing; browser console and server logs are clean. A `FirstChanceException` hook is the only evidence of the `InvalidOperationException`.\\n5. Full reload of `/crash`: same dead result (Auto stays on WASM once cached).\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nOnly observable via `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.FirstChanceException`:\\n`System.InvalidOperationException: Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.`\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.302\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n- ASP.NET Core version: 10.0.10 (behavior also reproduced on 10.0.9).\\n- Existing-issue search: `AddRootComponentAsync`, `OnUpdateRootComponents`, \\u0026#34;auto mode fallback\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;interactive auto stuck static\\u0026#34; — closest is #64508 ([Blazor] Unify root components initialization paths), which covers the divergent init paths but not the swallowed activation fault or the missing fallback.\\n- The same silent-discard exists for the `Update` operation.\\n- Happy to contribute a fix if you can indicate the preferred direction (await + log + error UI, vs. propagating the fault to enable Auto fallback).\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67980\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"alexaka1\",\"id\":22166651,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/alexaka1\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/22166651?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-23T14:16:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T07:22:48Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-27T02:07:49.361Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5081b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":25153,\"title\":\"Blazor WASM: RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore prevents use of ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath\",\"body\":\"I am building a Blazor WASM application that\\u0026#39;s connected to IdentityServer4.\\n\\nThe template for Single User Accounts provides ```LoginDisplay.razor``` which includes the following line:\\n\\n```\\n\\nAfter getting IdentityServer4 integrated via the following article, I noticed that the ```Register``` link simply redirected back to the Blazor app without any error messages.\\n\\nhttps://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/blazor/security/webassembly/hosted-with-identity-server?view=aspnetcore-3.1\\u0026amp;tabs=visual-studio\\n\\nIt wasn\\u0026#39;t clear what the ```RemoteAuthenticatorView``` was doing, so I dug into the code and came across the following:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs#L356\\n\\nIt\\u0026#39;s clear that ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` is being used for the redirect, but there is no documentation describing this. After setting the value to my external identity site ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` (different site entirely), I was presented with ```Sorry, there\\u0026#39;s nothing at this address.``` in the Blazor app. \\n\\nLooking closer at the above line of code, the ```.PathAndQuery``` piece at the end prevents ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` from ever being outside the Blazor app.\\n\\nAs a result, setting ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` to ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` executes a redirect to ```https://localhost:44357/Identity/Account/Register``` (my Blazor app).\\n\\nPlease confirm that this is a bug.\\n\\nEdit: ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteProfilePath``` seems to have the same issue.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/25153\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"hallidev\",\"id\":16142069,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/hallidev\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/16142069?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\",\"affected-most\",\"severity-minor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-auth\",\"triaged\",\"Pillar: Cloud Integration\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":17,\"+1\":9,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":3,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":3,\"eyes\":2},\"created_at\":\"2020-08-22T17:46:27Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-26T13:02:51Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Try to authentication/logout endpoint.\\n\\n**Additional context**\\n\\n- DOTNET 10\\n- Template: https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/tree/main/10.0/BlazorWebAppOidcBffAuto\\n\\nIs InteractiveWebAssembly not supported with the sample codes, or there any different changes we need to do?\\n\\n(cc: @guardrex https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/issues/642)\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65368\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Schoof-T\",\"id\":2319986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Schoof-T\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2319986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-auth\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\",\"Needs: Repro\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-02-09T12:00:32Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-19T07:44:43Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n * Render batches are communicated to JS via zero-copy shared memory rather than by serialization\\n * Events triggered from JS are always processed synchronously by .NET, so there\\u0026#39;s no need to queue them\\n\\nAt first glance, it appears to work with `true`, but that\\u0026#39;s a mirage: it does *not* guarantee correctness in that mode, because the core single-threadedness assumption is violated. For example, JS might raise event 2 before event 1 finished processing, and by the time event 1 is done, there might not even be an event 2 handler any more and then you have an error.\\n\\n### Why we\\u0026#39;re only just encountering this now\\n\\n1. We didn\\u0026#39;t have multithreading before\\n2. Even to the extent that we did have an early preview of multithreading, it worked by running .NET on the browser UI thread, so we could define that as the sync context and then all the same assumptions would remain valid within that sync context. But now .NET WebAssembly has just moved to the new \\u0026#34;deputy thread\\u0026#34; multithreading model (i.e., all .NET code is on a background worker), these assumptions are no longer valid (e.g., because the UI thread\\u0026#39;s JS can no longer communicate with .NET in a synchronous, blocking manner).\\n\\n### Ensuring correctness\\n\\nWe\\u0026#39;ve already solved all these problems in our other hosting environments, Server and WebView, because they\\u0026#39;ve always been innately asynchronous from the beginning. We would need to generalize/port all these mechanisms so they are shared with or copied by the WebAssembly renderer, JS interop, eventing system, etc.:\\n\\n- [ ] Change rendering to serialize renderbatches to JS instead of doing shared-memory reads\\n- [ ] Change the rendering flow so that the renderer\\u0026#39;s `UpdateDisplayAsync` returns a `Task` that doesn\\u0026#39;t complete until the JS side sends back an explicit acknowledgement of that renderbatch\\n- [ ] Review JS interop to make sure any low-level assumptions we\\u0026#39;ve made about synchrony during the internals of message passing are replaced by async assumptions\\n- [ ] Do the above without changing things for the **single-threaded** WebAssembly flavour, since (1) it would be breaking if for example synchronous UI updates became async, and (2) those perf optimizations are there for a reason, and we don\\u0026#39;t want to make rendering many times more expensive in cases where you\\u0026#39;d be serializing huge strings, for example. It\\u0026#39;s OK to have significant behavioral and performance changes when people opt into multithreading, but not when they don\\u0026#39;t.\\n\\n### Approach\\n\\nAs a broad strategy, I think we can:\\n\\n * Factor out some new `WebRenderer` subclass called something like `AsyncWebRenderer` that holds the common logic around serializing renderbatches and accepting the async renderbatch acknowledgements from JS. This can then be used by all of Server, WebView, and multithreaded-WebAssembly.\\n * Use our WebView implementation as the reference for how a complete, async-safe rendering and eventing model should work, because this was more recently implemented than Server and is generally simpler and cleaner. There\\u0026#39;s not a huge amount of code in it, really. If some extra work is needed to queue event notifications, for example, we should see that clearly from the WebView code.\\n\\nI suspect it\\u0026#39;s not necessary to have two different builds of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly`. The total amount of code that should differ between the threaded and not-threaded won\\u0026#39;t be very much. I expect we can just have two different `Renderer` subclasses and some if/else branches in the JS code.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54365\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"triaged\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-threading\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":26,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":47,\"+1\":30,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":17,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2024-03-05T10:02:51Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-04-21T00:06:24Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":true,\"has_children\":false,\"parent\":{\"number\":17730,\"title\":\"Real multithreading in Blazor WebAssembly\",\"state\":\"OPEN\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/17730\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"},\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

When navigating to `/error`, the Error page is rendered statically on the server, then when the client app starts, overwrites the Error page with the NotFound page content on the client. \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe default project should demonstrate how to mix server-rendered and client-rendered content properly in the same app. Currently, the default project itself demonstrates mixing the render modes incorrectly.\\n\\nWhile putting `@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` can be considered a workaround, it is undesirable: the layout of the application itself might still be using WebAssembly for even simple interactivity, like collapsing menus. `ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting` bypasses starting the WebAssembly runtime altogether.\\n\\nPossible solutions:\\n- Mark server-rendered content to persist on the client after client interactive routing kicks in. Possibly a marker attribute on the element, a directive, or an `@attribute` similar to `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute`.\\n- Allow `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute` to actually initialize the WebAssembly app, but leave the components marked with this attribute as-is in the DOM. Consider renaming the attribute if so. This might be easy to do using similar mechanics as seen in `PersistentState`\\n- Allow customizing the `Router`. For example, allow a behavior that lets the router \\u0026#34;keep\\u0026#34; the content as-is when a navigation event occurs, by overriding/passing `OnNavigatingAsync` or similar, or by inheriting from the built-in `Router`.\\n- Allow supplying a custom `Router` altogether. This would also allow multiple additional scenarios if community-built routers were to show up: handling localization in the URL, multiple hierarchic routers, etc.\\n- Allow rendering content on the server and let the client WebAssembly app \\u0026#34;consume\\u0026#34; the rendered static HTML as interactive. This might be a stretch, but for some simple cases, it can work.\\n- Modify/implement a new `RenderMode` that allows server-client handoff.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n`dotnet new blazor --name BlazorSSRCSR --all-interactive --interactivity WebAssembly`\\n`cd BlazorSSRCSR`\\n`dotnet run`\\n\\nNavigate to the created app\\u0026#39;s `/error` endpoint. The endpoint will show the server side error, then after a short time, the client side router overwrites the content with the client side `NotFound` page content.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.100-rc.1.25451.107\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nThis is NOT the same as similar (possibly slightly related) issues:\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38128\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/42561\\n\\nNote that there\\u0026#39;s also the implication that if this is done, \\u0026#34;mixing\\u0026#34; render modes across a hierarchy might become possible. That would also require the user be able to set `RenderMode` to `Static` explicitly, which is currently not possible because it\\u0026#39;s not even defined in `RenderMode`: it\\u0026#39;s condered `Static` rendering when the `RenderMode` evaluates to `null`.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/63842\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"yugabe\",\"id\":14803737,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/yugabe\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/14803737?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-09-26T13:34:52Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-02-13T11:20:42Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

A single app load emits multiple Information-level lines per HTTP request through the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointMiddleware`, and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticAssets.StaticAssetsInvoker` categories. Because a Blazor WebAssembly boot pulls many assets, this results in hundreds of log lines for a single page load.\\n\\nThe equivalent standalone Blazor WebAssembly app on .NET 10 starts up with only a handful of log lines and stays quiet during normal browsing.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nA freshly created standalone Blazor WebAssembly app should have a console log volume comparable to the .NET 10 experience — roughly: startup banner, listening URL, hosting environment, content root, and not much else during normal dev-time browsing.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n1. Install the .NET 11 Preview 5 SDK (`11.0.100-preview.5.26272.118`).\\n2. `dotnet new blazorwasm -o WasmTest`\\n3. `cd WasmTest`\\n4. `dotnet run`\\n5. Open `http://localhost:/` in a browser.\\n6. Observe the console output.\\n\\nPer-request output (one example request, repeated for every asset):\\n\\n```\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[1]\\n      Request starting HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/ - - -\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointMiddleware[0]\\n      Executing endpoint \\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.RouteEndpoint\\u0026#39;\\u0026#39;\\ninfo: Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticAssets.StaticAssetsInvoker[2]\\n      Sending file. I configured the MSAL cache to use localStorage by setting the CacheLocation in MsalProviderOptions like this:\\n\\n```\\nbuilder.Services.AddMsalAuthentication(options =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    options.ProviderOptions.Cache.CacheLocation = \\u0026#34;localStorage\\u0026#34;;\\n    // other config...\\n});\\n```\\n\\nThis works well initially—tokens are stored and retrieved as expected. However, after a few hours (presumably when the token expires), the app doesn\\u0026#39;t seem to automatically acquire a new token. Even when I try to sign out manually using:\\n\\n`await SignOutManager.SetSignOutState();`\\n\\n...any pages decorated with `[Authorize]` still redirect to the NotAuthorized view. The only workaround I’ve found is to manually clear localStorage in the browser, which obviously isn’t ideal.\\n\\nAny insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe expected behavior when using localStorage as the cacheLocation in a Blazor WebAssembly app with MSAL should be:\\n\\n- **Persistent Token Storage**: Tokens (ID, access, and refresh) should persist across browser sessions as long as they are valid and not manually cleared, since localStorage is not cleared on tab or browser close.\\n- **Automatic Silent Token Renewal**: When an access token expires, MSAL should attempt to silently acquire a new token using the refresh token (if available and valid), without requiring user interaction.\\n- **Graceful Sign-Out**: Calling SignOutManager.SetSignOutState() should clear the authentication state and redirect the user appropriately. After sign-out, protected routes decorated with [Authorize] should redirect to the login page or a configured fallback, not remain stuck on a NotAuthorized view.\\n- **No Manual Storage Clearing Required**: Users should not need to manually clear localStorage to resolve expired token issues. The library should handle token lifecycle management internally.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n1. Run a Blazor wasm project with Microsoft.Authentication.WebAssembly.Msal\\n```\\nservices.AddMsalAuthentication(remoteAuthenticationOptions =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    remoteAuthenticationOptions.ProviderOptions.Cache.CacheLocation = \\u0026#34;localStorage\\u0026#34;;\\n    webAssemblyHostBuilder.Configuration.Bind(\\n        \\u0026#34;AzureAd\\u0026#34;,\\n        remoteAuthenticationOptions.ProviderOptions.Authentication\\n    );\\n});\\n```\\n\\n2. appsettings.json with `AzureAd` section:\\n```\\n\\u0026#34;AzureAd\\u0026#34;: {\\n  \\u0026#34;Authority\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;Your-Authority\\u0026#34;,\\n  \\u0026#34;ClientId\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;Your-ClientId\\u0026#34;,\\n  \\u0026#34;ValidateAuthority\\u0026#34;: true\\n}\\n```\\n\\n3. Login into the project and wait until the token is expired.\\n4. Go back to the page and you\\u0026#39;ll not be able to navigate through the page. Token has not been correctly refreshed.\\n\\nNeed to manually clean localStorage to force app to get a new token.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n9.0.204\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/61960\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"galehost\",\"id\":138874295,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/galehost\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/138874295?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"investigate\",\"area-auth\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":2,\"+1\":2,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-05-16T10:10:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-03T12:01:44Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

We should light the feature up end to end for circuits so that a long-lived circuit can pick up a refreshed principal instead of being torn down when the token expires.\\n\\nThis is the Blazor half of the long-standing https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/5297.\\n\\n## What SignalR gives us today\\n\\nServer (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections` / `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR`):\\n\\n- `HttpConnectionDispatcherOptions.EnableAuthenticationRefresh`\\n- An internal `/refresh` endpoint stamped with the same auth metadata/conventions as the connection endpoint\\n- `tokenLifetimeSeconds` in the negotiate payload when the auth ticket has an expiration\\n- `HttpConnectionDispatcherOptions.OnAuthenticationRefresh` (`AuthenticationRefreshContext` -\\u0026gt; `ValueTask`) to accept/reject the refreshed principal\\n- `virtual Task Hub.OnAuthenticationRefreshedAsync()`, invoked after the connection user state has been applied, serialized through `ActiveInvocationLimit`\\n- `HubCallerContext.User` snapshotting, so in-flight hub methods keep the principal they started with\\n- Connection abort if the `UserIdentifier` changes\\n\\nJS client (`@microsoft/signalr`):\\n\\n- `HubConnection.refreshAuthentication(): Promise`\\n- Automatic re-arming of refresh based on the returned token lifetime, including after reconnect\\n\\n## Proposed work\\n\\n### 1. `ComponentHub.OnAuthenticationRefreshedAsync`\\n\\nOverride the new hub callback and flow the refreshed principal into the circuit, reusing the existing `CircuitHost.SetCircuitUser` path so `IHostEnvironmentAuthenticationStateProvider` / `ServerAuthenticationStateProvider` is updated and components re-render with the new `AuthenticationState`.\\n\\nThere is already a prototype of exactly this (plus unit tests) at [REDACTED] on `origin/copilot/67111-update-authenticationstateprovider`:\\n\\n```csharp\\npublic override Task OnAuthenticationRefreshedAsync()\\n{\\n    var circuitHost = _circuitHandleRegistry.GetCircuit(Context.Items, CircuitKey);\\n    if (circuitHost == null)\\n    {\\n        // No circuit is associated with this connection yet, so there is nothing to update.\\n        return Task.CompletedTask;\\n    }\\n\\n    circuitHost.SetCircuitUser(Context.User);\\n    return Task.CompletedTask;\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThat commit predates the final API shape/merge, so it needs to be rebased and re-validated against `main`.\\n\\n### 2. Opt-in configuration for the Blazor endpoint\\n\\nDecide how apps turn this on. `MapBlazorHub(..., Action)` and `ServerComponentsEndpointOptions.ConfigureConnection` already let an app set `EnableAuthenticationRefresh` and `OnAuthenticationRefresh` manually, but we should decide whether:\\n\\n- it stays purely manual,\\n- we surface a first-class option on `CircuitOptions` / `ServerComponentsEndpointOptions`, and/or\\n- we enable it by default when `CloseOnAuthenticationExpiration` is set.\\n\\n### 3. Blazor JS client wiring\\n\\n`blazor.server.js` / `blazor.web.js` build the `HubConnection` internally, so app code can\\u0026#39;t call `refreshAuthentication()` on it. We need to decide the public surface for triggering a refresh from the Blazor client — for example an option on `Blazor.start({ circuit: ... })` to supply a token factory and/or enable automatic refresh, or an exposed `Blazor.refreshAuthentication()`.\\n\\n### 4. Interaction with existing Blazor auth pieces\\n\\n- `RevalidatingServerAuthenticationStateProvider` / `RevalidatingAuthenticationStateProvider` — should a successful refresh reset the revalidation loop, and should revalidation failure still terminate the circuit?\\n- `CloseOnAuthenticationExpiration` on the circuit endpoint — a refresh must extend the connection\\u0026#39;s auth expiration rather than let the circuit be closed.\\n- `AuthenticationStateProvider` change notifications reaching ``, `[Authorize]`-protected routable components, and `PersistentAuthenticationStateProvider` for interactive WASM in a Blazor Web App.\\n- Circuit pause/resume and stateful reconnect: the refreshed principal must survive, and a reconnect must not silently revert to the original principal.\\n- `UserIdentifier` change aborts the connection at the SignalR layer — confirm the circuit termination path is graceful and produces a sensible client-side experience.\\n\\n### 5. Tests + docs\\n\\n- Unit tests on `ComponentHub` (already drafted in the prototype commit).\\n- E2E test covering: start circuit with a short-lived token, refresh, assert `` observes the new claims without a reconnect.\\n- Template/docs guidance for the bearer-token hosting scenarios this targets.\\n\\n## Notes\\n\\n- The commit in question is on a stale branch and uses `SetCircuitUser` directly; the merged SignalR API name is `OnAuthenticationRefreshedAsync`, so the prototype lines up, but everything else around it needs revisiting.\\n- Windows authentication refresh is explicitly rejected by SignalR, so that scenario is out of scope here.\\n\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68170\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"javiercn\",\"id\":6995051,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/javiercn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6995051?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"api-proposal\"],\"assignees\":[\"kotlarmilos\"],\"milestone\":\"11.0-rc1\",\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-03T17:57:02Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-12T08:37:03Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-08-12T08:37:03Z\",\"closed_by\":\"kotlarmilos\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":68221,\"title\":\"[Blazor] Propagate SignalR authentication refresh to server circuits\",\"state\":\"MERGED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/68221\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

When `CloseOnAuthenticationExpiration` is enabled, the server closes the connection when the token expires and the client must reconnect. That can create a gap where messages are missed and connection-local state is disrupted.\\n\\nThis proposal adds an opt-in authentication-refresh flow for SignalR HTTP connections. The server can expose a `/refresh` endpoint for an existing connection, re-authenticate the request using the endpoint\\u0026#39;s normal authentication and authorization metadata, and update the connection\\u0026#39;s `ClaimsPrincipal` without disconnecting when the connection\\u0026#39;s refresh policy accepts the transition. Long Polling poll requests and stateful WebSocket reconnect requests use the same refresh policy when they present updated credentials.\\n\\nThe refreshed principal is published to future hub invocations and to `Hub.OnAuthenticationRefreshedAsync`. SignalR user routing is deliberately not rekeyed: `HubCallerContext.UserIdentifier` and `Clients.User(...)` routing retain the connection-start identity, while group membership is left unchanged by refresh. The default SignalR policy rejects a refresh that maps to a different user identifier. A component that does not use SignalR user routing, such as Blazor\\u0026#39;s `ComponentHub`, can replace that policy and accept authenticated/anonymous identity transitions while still keeping the connection\\u0026#39;s routing identifier fixed.\\n\\nSee #5297 for more context.\\n\\n## Implementation Status\\n\\nThe implementation is on `main`; the APIs below remain unshipped:\\n\\n- #67111 added the server and .NET client refresh flow.\\n- #67964 added the TypeScript client APIs.\\n- #68459 added the replaceable transition policy, monotonic publication, timer hardening, fixed user-routing semantics, and Blazor integration.\\n\\nThe proposal below reflects the current implementation after those changes.\\n\\nBlazor now enables authentication refresh on both its server endpoint and internal TypeScript `HubConnection`, accepts identity transitions at the circuit layer, and updates the circuit authentication state after a refresh. A lifecycle-triggered Blazor follow-up for the anonymous-to-authenticated case is not part of this proposal or current `main`: an anonymous authentication state has no reported token lifetime, so the generic SignalR client intentionally has no timer to trigger a later refresh.\\n\\n## Proposed API\\n\\n```diff\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections;\\n\\npublic class HttpConnectionDispatcherOptions\\n{\\n+    public bool EnableAuthenticationRefresh { get; set; }\\n+    public Func\\u0026gt;? OnAuthenticationRefresh { get; set; }\\n}\\n\\n+public sealed class AuthenticationRefreshContext\\n+{\\n+    public required HttpContext HttpContext { get; init; }\\n+    public required string ConnectionId { get; init; }\\n+    public required ClaimsPrincipal PreviousUser { get; init; }\\n+    public required ClaimsPrincipal NewUser { get; init; }\\n+    public required DateTimeOffset NewExpiration { get; init; }\\n+}\\n+\\n+public sealed class AuthenticationRefreshMetadata\\n+{\\n+}\\n```\\n\\n```diff\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Connections;\\n\\npublic class NegotiationResponse\\n{\\n+    public TimeSpan? TokenLifetime { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```diff\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Connections.Features;\\n\\n+public interface IAuthenticationRefreshFeature\\n+{\\n+    TimeSpan? InitialTokenLifetime { get; }\\n+    Task RefreshAuthenticationAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);\\n+}\\n+\\n+public interface IConnectionUserRefreshFeature\\n+{\\n+    Func? OnUserRefreshing { get; set; }\\n+    IDisposable OnUserRefreshed(Action callback, object? state);\\n+}\\n```\\n\\n`OnUserRefreshing` is the single replaceable feature-level pre-publication callback. It runs synchronously while the connection user update is locked and must return `true` for the update to proceed. Setting it replaces the previous callback; setting it to `null` restores the feature implementation\\u0026#39;s secure default. Exceptions reject the update. The callback must complete quickly and must not block or re-enter the user update.\\n\\n`OnUserRefreshed` is a post-publication notification. It does not expose the previous principal because resources owned by that principal, such as a `WindowsIdentity` handle, may already have been disposed by the time an asynchronous consumer observes the notification.\\n\\n```diff\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client;\\n\\npublic class HubConnection\\n{\\n+    public Task RefreshAuthenticationAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);\\n}\\n\\n+public sealed class AuthenticationRefreshOptions\\n+{\\n+    public bool EnableAutoRefresh { get; set; } = true;\\n+    public TimeSpan RefreshBeforeExpiration { get; set; } = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);\\n+    public Func? OnAuthenticationRefreshed { get; set; }\\n+    public Func? OnAuthenticationRefreshFailed { get; set; }\\n+}\\n+\\n+public sealed class AuthenticationRefreshedContext\\n+{\\n+    public HubConnection HubConnection { get; }\\n+    public TimeSpan? NewTokenLifetime { get; }\\n+    public DateTimeOffset RefreshedAt { get; }\\n+}\\n+\\n+public sealed class AuthenticationRefreshFailedContext\\n+{\\n+    public HubConnection HubConnection { get; }\\n+    public Exception Exception { get; }\\n+}\\n\\npublic static class HubConnectionBuilderExtensions\\n{\\n+    public static IHubConnectionBuilder WithAuthenticationRefresh(\\n+        this IHubConnectionBuilder hubConnectionBuilder,\\n+        Action configure);\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```diff\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR;\\n\\npublic abstract class Hub\\n{\\n+    public virtual Task OnAuthenticationRefreshedAsync();\\n}\\n```\\n\\n```diff\\n// @microsoft/signalr\\n\\n+export interface IAuthenticationRefreshOptions {\\n+    enableAutoRefresh?: boolean;\\n+    refreshBeforeExpirationInMilliseconds?: number;\\n+    onAuthenticationRefreshed?(context: AuthenticationRefreshedContext): void | Promise;\\n+    onAuthenticationRefreshFailed?(context: AuthenticationRefreshFailedContext): void | Promise;\\n+}\\n+\\n+export interface AuthenticationRefreshedContext {\\n+    connection: HubConnection;\\n+    newTokenLifetimeInSeconds?: number;\\n+    refreshedAt: Date;\\n+}\\n+\\n+export interface AuthenticationRefreshFailedContext {\\n+    connection: HubConnection;\\n+    error: Error;\\n+}\\n\\nexport class HubConnectionBuilder {\\n+    withAuthenticationRefresh(options: IAuthenticationRefreshOptions = {}): HubConnectionBuilder;\\n}\\n\\nexport class HubConnection {\\n+    refreshAuthentication(): Promise;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Usage Examples\\n\\nEnable authentication refresh on the server:\\n\\n```csharp\\napp.MapHub(\\u0026#34;/chat\\u0026#34;, options =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    options.EnableAuthenticationRefresh = true;\\n\\n Please describe the problem.\\n\\nWhen using Blazor WASM, OAuth session logout notifications can be handled using `check_session_iframe` as supported by oidc-client and supported Identity Providers like [Identity Server](https://docs.duendesoftware.com/identityserver/v5/ui/logout/notification/#browser-based-javascript-clients). This OAuth functionality allows WASM tabs to be notified when the remote session at the Identity Provider is terminated and allows the WASM to log the user out. The default AuthenticationService.js implementation in asp.net core supports this functionality and the check session iFrame is working as expected. However, when the AuthenticationService.js notices that the session has been terminated through the JS interop, it does not update the UI. Instead the user is still shown an interface that appears as if they are logged in.\\n\\n### Describe the solution you\\u0026#39;d like\\n\\nAn ideal solution would be to support the native oidc-client events like `userUnloaded` with the `addUserUnloaded(...)` function. Doing this would allow us to redirect the user as the WASM application deems necessary. We cannot use back channel notifications at this time so having the ability to use the check session front channel is the only path forward. We are also open to other approaches to achieve this if you have any suggestions.\\n\\nWe are also open to contributing to the asp.net core AuthenticationService.ts to support specifying custom callbacks on the native oidc-client events. If we wrote this feature and opened a PR, would asp.net core be open to  merge that into the code base?\\n\\n### Additional context\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;m attaching a video screenshot of the current series of calls as well as one solution we used by adding the `userUnloaded` call. If you would be open to accepting a PR for this, we could look to make this more generic to use callbacks.\\n\\nThis screenshot has a demo Blazor WASM app, an IdentityServer Identity Provider, and a second client. The user is logged into the WASM and the second client through the IdP. [2026-08-27T02:08:21.969Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 6881b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":48404,\"title\":\"Blazor WebAssembly integration with Msal.js fails fatally when changing Authority URL\",\"body\":\"### Is there an existing issue for this?\\n\\n- [X] I have searched the existing issues\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\nThe `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Authentication` library packages a JS file - `AuthenticationService.ts` that is a shim between the library code and MSAL.js.  This service makes assumptions about the number of accounts cached by the MSAL.js service and their validity with the currently configured authority.  For example, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Components/WebAssembly/Authentication.Msal/src/Interop/AuthenticationService.ts#LL152C55-L152C55\\n\\nThe `getAccount()` method linked above is used during the login process and when the Authority is changed between app releases,  anyone with existing cached authentication details will get stuck in an infinite login loop.\\n\\nThe behaviour experienced in `net 6` vs `net 7` are slightly different. In net 6, the application seems to loop indefinitely - being unable to complete a code grant flow, failing on the step where the token is retrieved from the \\u0026#34;/token\\u0026#34; endpoint. In net 7 the system seems to get past this point, but the result is that two sets of credentials are cached in the browser `localStorage`. Using `IAccessTokenProvider` to retrieve a token for use with downstream APIs always returns \\u0026#34;RedirectRequired\\u0026#34; so the token is unreachable from the app code.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nMSAL interop services should be able to correctly navigate circumstances where there are cached credentials that are out of context for the current login process, rather than assuming if there are \\u0026#34;any accounts available, we can just use the first one\\u0026#34;.\\n\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n- Configure an AAD B2C tenant in the normal way.\\n- Add Front Door with and configure 2 custom domain names\\n- Update AAD to support access from the new custom domain names\\n\\nYou will now have 3 valid \\u0026#34;authority\\u0026#34; names to use when accessing B2C.\\n\\n- Using the standard Blazor WASM template, connect to B2C and use the default B2C authority urls\\n- Login normally, close the browser\\n- Update the Authority in the settings file to use the custom domain name\\n- Start up the WASM app again and you will no longer be able to log in (net6) or you will be constantly directed to re-login by the IAccessTokenProvider (net7)\\n\\nLogging out removes all items from the cache (which is also a bug) which does resolve the issue, but only because all the cache is dumped. It\\u0026#39;s not reasonable to expect everyday users of websites to know how to clear localStorage. Even clearing the browser cache does not resolve the problem.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\nnet6 and net7\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nWe have some workarounds in place where we check the currently configured authorities and programatically cleanup the localStorage. This permanently resolves the issue but also does not provide for the support of multiple logins in localStorage or multiple Authorities.\\n\\nWhether it\\u0026#39;s reasonable for multiple identities to be cached at the same time is a matter for debate. If it\\u0026#39;s not reasonable then the MSAL.js should take steps to remove accounts from the wrong Authority from the cache rather than blindly loading them. If it is reasonable then \\u0026#34;Authentication.MSAL\\u0026#34; should provide the necessary overloads to handle this situation gracefully. Either way there is a bug that needs to be fixed here, IMHO.\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48404\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"richardhauer\",\"id\":225807,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/richardhauer\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/225807?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"Needs: Author Feedback\",\"area-blazor\",\"Status: No Recent Activity\"],\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2023-05-24T06:50:03Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2023-07-01T03:00:44Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2023-06-01T00:00:53Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

It\\u0026#39;s difficult to reproduce, but I saw it happening on a iPhone with Chrome. What I saw is that the url only consisted of `https://xxx.com/authentication/login-callback` resulting in the app being stuck on infinite \\u0026#39;logging-in\\u0026#39;, because with that url the masl.js libarary only returns `operation completed` which is not handled in the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Authentication.RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogInCallback`.\\n\\nI created the following fix by overriding the \\u0026#39;RemoteAuthenticatorView\\u0026#39;, but would like to get your opinion about the possible risks\\\\implications of this and maybe this will need to be fixed in the original \\u0026#39;RemoteAuthenticationView\\u0026#39; aswell.\\n\\n```\\npublic sealed class AuthenticatorViewEx : RemoteAuthenticatorView\\n{\\n    [Inject] internal NavigationManager Navigation { get; set; }\\n    [Inject] internal AuthenticationStateProvider AuthenticationStateProvider { get; set; }\\n\\n    protected override async Task OnParametersSetAsync()\\n    {\\n        await base.OnParametersSetAsync();\\n\\n        // Fix stuck in login-callback =\\u0026gt; redirect to home or login\\n        if (Action == RemoteAuthenticationActions.LogInCallback \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; safeoutputs.description: WRITE-ONCE: do NOT call this tool with empty or placeholder arguments to probe or discover its schema — the required `body` field is listed in this schema; if you are not ready to post a real comment, call `noop` instead. Adds a comment to an existing GitHub issue, pull request, or discussion. Use this to provide feedback, answer questions, or add information to an existing conversation. For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 comment(s) can be added. Target: *. This tool records a real comment intent. Do not use it for placeholder comments, auth checks, or probing. Call it only when the final comment body is ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.
safeoutputs.name: add_comment

safeoutputs.description: Add labels to an existing GitHub issue or pull request for categorization and filtering. Labels must already exist in the repository. For creating new issues with labels, use create_issue with the labels property instead. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 3 label(s) can be added. Only these labels are allowed: ["area-auth" "area-blazor" "area-commandlinetools" "area-dataprotection" "area-grpc" "area-healthchecks" "area-hosting" "area-identity" "area-infrastructure" "area-middleware" "area-minimal" "area-mvc" "area-networking" "area-perf" "area-routing" "area-security" "area-signalr" "area-ui-rendering" "area-unified-build" "by-design" "question" "external" "docs" "api-proposal" "test-failure" "performance"]. INTENT ENCOURAGED: Include rationale (string, max 280 chars) and confidence (exactly one of: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) with each call. These fields are optional but strongly encouraged — they improve transparency and should normally be included. Use suggest: true alongside rationale and confidence to route for human review.

safeoutputs.description: Remove labels from an existing GitHub issue or pull request. Silently skips labels that don't exist on the item. Use this to clean up labels or manage label lifecycles (e.g., removing 'needs-review' after review is complete). CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 label(s) can be removed. Only these labels can be removed: [needs-area-label].
safeoutputs.name: remove_labels

safeoutputs.description: Report that a tool or capability needed to complete the task is not available, or share any information you deem important about missing functionality or limitations. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because the required functionality is missing or access is restricted. When a bash command is blocked by security policy, call this tool with reason set to "security".
safeoutputs.name: missing_tool

safeoutputs.description: Log a transparency message when no significant actions are needed. Use this to confirm workflow completion and provide visibility when analysis is complete but no changes or outputs are required (e.g., 'No issues found', 'All checks passed'). This ensures the workflow produces human-visible output even when no other actions are taken.

safeoutputs.description: Report that data or information needed to complete the task is not available. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because required data, context, or information is missing.

safeoutputs.description: Signal that the task could not be completed due to an infrastructure or tool failure (e.g., MCP server crash, missing authentication, inaccessible repository). Use this when required tools or data are unavailable and the task cannot be meaningfully performed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running. Provide a specific reason and optional details so downstream issue aggregation can preserve complete incomplete-signal context. The workflow framework will treat this as a failure signal even when the agent exits successfully.
